chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: Refusing and then accepting the invitation to tour Europe
summary: Cobb explains he turned down European tours while his wife lived, until his mother urged him to answer, and in 1973 the organizers arranged help for him.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You done talked -- you don't talked out?
Well, I have some things I want to talk about.
Now, just -- before we do that, let's just finish -- now, so you work around Houston until the (inaudible) present day.
Now, so now, when did you come up to New York and went to Nice -- when was that, two years ago?
I went to Nice last year for the first time. But may I give you the starting point of this?
Yes, but I was just trying to figure when you started to come out of Houston.

Oh, I started before last year, started before Nice. That's what I want to tell you. They kept calling me and writing me to come to Europe on a tour. My wife is passed now, and before she passed I didn't go and I didn't accept so because she didn't want to go, and I didn't have anybody to go with me in my physical condition. So (inaudible) my mother-- they invited me to (inaudible) the Montreux situation, and I told them I'm busy. I wasn't that busy. So my mother finally said to me, she said, Baby, they going to stop inviting you if you don't tell them something. Tell them what
it is." So I said okay. She woke me up. So I got up and I wrote them a letter, and I gave them the whole rundown. I laid my cards on the table.

They wrote me back and said they'd (inaudible) if they didn't know nothing about that; I'd told them that five, six years ago. So then they said, "We're going to have somebody to help you here. You don't have to worry about it." So I accepted the next one. The first one was '73, and when I got there, they had somebody to take care, in fact, took care of me so well until the cat wanted to come up and make me eat what I didn't want to eat.
Honestly. That's how nice they were.
